text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Water resources minister Aliyu Yelwa tells the northern states of Nigeria to prepare for possible drought in the region in the year 2003, which is the next stop in a 10-year cycle of scanty rains that last occured in 1993.
- British Petroleum, Statoil alliance begin to demobilise some of their staff in Nigeria due to failure to find oil after four years of exploration in the country's offshore waters.
- Federal government courts new British government, appeals against imposing sanctions on Nigeria.
- Nigerian unit of oil giant Shell refutes charges from U.S. non-governmental organisations that it caused ecological and other havoc in Ogoniland.

- Mergers and acquisitions, not liquidation, appears to be favoured by the regulatory authorities for dealing with the 43 distressed banks that have failed to meet a March 31, 1997 deadline to recapitalise.
- Lagos zone of failed banks tribunals orders 14 companies to pay up 509 million naira owed distressed banks by Wednesday next week.
- Gunmen on Thursday shot and killed a former commissioner (minister) in the eastern Enugu state, Charles Nnachetam and stole his luxury car.
- Cocoa association of Nigeria plans to boost production of the crop in the country, says its chairman Bayo Iyaniwura.
- Oil firms operating in Nigeria owe federal government 22 billion in unpaid withholding taxes, according to the government consultant on petroleum taxes, Jimoh Ibrahim.
- Weekly demand for forex falls to $80.09 million from $109.58 million last week following a declaration by the authorities that there are no plan to devalue the local currency.
- Shell oil comapny says it will phase out gas flaring in Nigeria by the year 2008.
- A plane carrying 50 passengers to the capital Abuja from Lagos on Thursday was forced to turn back and make an emergency landing because it developed an engine problem few minutes after take-off.
